updates.sentence:
September 4, 1917: 60 days at Occoquan.

Turning Point Suffragist Memorial reports that Annie D. (Mrs. William) Chisholm was released on personal bond after 12 days. The 60 days was the imposed sentence, not the documented period served. Exact release day remains unresolved.

operations.research_note: Individually named memorial entry explicitly distinguishes twelve days before bond from sixty-day imposed sentence in Stevens. Correct the previous sixty actual days; do not calculate a release day by subtraction.

expected.description: Mrs. William Chisholm was a member of the National Woman's Party and one of the "Silent Sentinels" imprisoned during the 1917-1919 campaign to picket the Wilson White House for woman suffrage. Doris Stevens recorded her term as: September 4, 1917: 60 days at Occoquan.

operations.research_note: Alexander Street scholarly biographical sketch by Jayce Oran and David Baker identifies Anne Dorris as William Wallace Chisholm’s wife and dates death to January 1918, citing Tyrone Daily Herald Jan9,1918 p3.
